user_confirms.question: Does the feature work reliably for the users it is for, with known blocking bugs fixed and onboarding tried by real users?
Can the product, support and sign-up path take about 410 sessions on launch day (the planning target), with headroom for 520?
Are help docs or an FAQ for the feature ready, and is someone answering questions on launch day?
Are the launch page copy, a demo video, social images and the email drafts ready? A press kit only if press is part of the plan.

Warm the email list with two ordinary sends before the launch email.
Re-run the mobile page speed check on the launch page.
timeline.phase_note: A tier 1 feature uses three phases (build-up, launch day and momentum), so foundation, seeding and iteration are not planned.

channel_plan.plan: The site and organic search carry most traffic, but the email list is cold: building and warming it is the first owned task. Point every rented and borrowed link at the waitlist.

YouTube is the only network with real reach (53,000 views in 90 days on channel 1, which gained subscribers). Make the launch demo a YouTube video. Channel 2 lost more subscribers than it gained, and the Facebook Page has 7 followers: post there, but don't count on it. In the April moment, instagram.com was the second source as GA4 reports it (98 of 350 sessions, just behind (direct)), and l.instagram.com was fourth (49); no Instagram account is connected, so its reach is unknown.

The largest past moment was a one-source burst from a software directory (upside you can't count on, but worth asking for again). Line up directory listings and partner mentions for launch week; AI assistants already send a few visits.

With the $2,000 budget: about $400 in the two weeks before (promote the build-up content to grow the waitlist), $1,000 in launch week (amplify the best-performing launch post), $600 over the next three weeks (retargeting launch visitors). No branded search: brand capture passes (average position 1.1). The baseline already gets paid traffic (Paid Search 18, Cross-network 36 sessions over the 5 baseline days), but no call in this run measures audience sizes, so whether a retargeting pool exists is unknown: check it in the ad platform before spending the pre-launch share, and spend less before launch if there is none.

launch_day_run_of_show.block: Before the morning peak (launch time zone)
launch_day_run_of_show.do: Systems check, publish the landing page update, the announcement post and the YouTube demo, switch on the in-app message, send the launch email to all users.
Post on YouTube, the Facebook Page and personal profiles; personal notes to early users and partners; reply to every comment.
Keep replying, share quotes as they come in, thank people who share. No second email: the list is cold.
Short progress post, public thanks, triage issues, plan day 2.

launch_day_sessions.formula: baseline 91 sessions a day x planning multiple 4.5 (stretch x 5.7)
launch_day_sessions.assumption: past moments predict the size of a spike only if the launch reaches a similar audience; the baseline is thin (5 days since tracking recovered)

targets.after_30_days: compare the 28 days after launch with this baseline for sessions, new users, key events and brand clicks; ask the user for activation, week-1 retention, paid conversions and NPS from the product, each against their own pre-launch figure and labelled 'from the user, not measured' (none was given for this run)
